title.narrative: Improved governance of labour market information systems in line with the latest labour statistics standards.

description.narrative: Mauritius faces challenges in ensuring fair and evidence-based wage and labour market policies. The current sector-based wage determination system shows inconsistencies, including unequal pay for similar occupations, administrative complexity and weak alignment with labour market dynamics. In parallel, labour market information remains fragmented across institutions, limiting its use for effective policy design and monitoring. Mauritius also seeks to strengthen labour market statistics through implementation of the 21st International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS) Resolution on statistics of the informal economy to improve the measurement of informality and labour market vulnerability. To address these challenges, the ILO supports Mauritius through an integrated strategy to strengthen wage-setting systems, labour market statistics and labour market information systems (LMIS). The intervention includes technical support for implementing the 21st ICLS Resolution, developing a national LMIS and Labour Market Observatory aligned with SADC regional initiatives, and conducting diagnostics and reform options for the wage determination system. The programme combines technical analysis, policy advice, capacity-building and tripartite social dialogue to improve coordination and dissemination of labour market data, including through digital tools. Expected results include stronger national capacity to produce and use labour market statistics in line with international standards, improved access to reliable labour market information, and more transparent and equitable wage policies. The intervention benefits workers, particularly those in vulnerable and low-paid employment, employers, policymakers, social partners, researchers and users of labour market statistics. The strategy is implemented with the Ministry of Labour and Industrial Relations, Statistics Mauritius and SADC partners, with support from the ILO.
